successCriteria.description: A self-profile read endpoint exists that returns HTTP 200 with the authenticated employee's profile, and the response body never contains `passwordHash` (the field is stripped before serialization).

The actor is resolved exclusively from `request.user` (never a client-supplied id); a missing/invalid authenticated user yields a 401 UnauthorizedError, matching the `resolveActor` behavior in `src/modules/leave/leave.routes.ts`.
`employeeRoutes` is exported from `src/modules/employee/index.ts` and mounted in `src/app.ts` alongside `authRoutes` and `balanceRoutes`, with `registerAuth(app)` still registered before the routes.
`AppError` failures (e.g. `NotFoundError` when the employee does not exist) are mapped to `{ error, code }` with the correct status via the `sendError` pattern, not a bare 500.

constraints: The service is resolved from `fastify.employeeService` when present, else `new EmployeeService(new PgEmployeeRepository())` — never hand-wire a different repository or bypass the repository pattern.
`passwordHash` must never be serialized into any response body; the profile returned to the caller is the `Employee` shape minus `passwordHash`.
The caller's identity comes only from `request.user` (populated by `registerAuth`); no client-supplied id, query param, or body field may select the employee.
This is a read-only operation — no transaction is opened and no write occurs.
outOfScope: Extending `scripts/smoke.js` with new authenticated stages (Phase 7b — Smoke check extension).
Unit/integration tests for auth, balance, and leave services (Phase 7c — Unit tests).
Creating or modifying `authRoutes`/`balanceRoutes`/`leaveRoutes` implementations — only mounting them in `src/app.ts` is in scope.

entityInvariants.invariant: `passwordHash` is a canonical field on the `Employee` entity (nullable) but is a write-only/never-serialized field: it may be read by the auth service for comparison but must never appear in any HTTP response body.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: The id is the authenticated actor's id from `request.user`; the route enforces authentication before invoking the service.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Throws NotFoundError('Employee not found') when no employee matches; the route maps it to 404 `{ error, code }`.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: The self-profile endpoint is authenticated (not in PUBLIC_PATHS); unauthenticated requests are rejected by the preHandler hook with 401.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: AppError is mapped via sendError to `{ error, code }` with the correct status; unexpected errors become 500.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Reuse the `resolveActor` pattern (validate `request.user`, throw `UnauthorizedError('Missing authenticated user')` / `'Invalid user role'`, return `{ id, role }`) exactly as implemented in the leave routes.
Reuse the `sendError` mapping (AppError → `{ error, code }` with `error.statusCode`; otherwise 500 `{ error: 'Internal Server Error' }`) exactly as in the leave routes.
The `Employee` entity returned by `getEmployeeById` includes `passwordHash: string | null`; the route must strip it before responding, matching the auth service's strip behavior.
`registerAuth(app)` must remain registered before route mounting so the preHandler hook populates `request.user` for the new endpoint.

integrationPoints.why: The route delegates profile lookup to the existing service method, which already throws NotFoundError when the employee is missing.
The authenticated actor id/role is supplied by the auth preHandler hook; the route reads it rather than trusting client input.
These sibling-phase routes are mounted in src/app.ts in this phase alongside employeeRoutes.
